name: Milk & Madu Beach Road
why_its_here: A spacious, palm-shaded all-day cafe on Batu Bolong beach road with a kids' play area, brunch classics and lava-stone pizzas, part of the well-known Milk & Madu group.
best_for: Families with young children and groups; brunch through to an easy early dinner, plus daily sunset sessions.
not_for: Couples seeking an intimate, quiet dining atmosphere.

name: Atlas Beach Club
spend: Day pass 300K - includes welcome drink, pool access, towel hire
why_its_here: A large beachfront entertainment complex on Jl. Pantai Berawa running four venues on one site: Beach Club, Super Club, Wellness Club and a padel club. Its own site markets it as the world's biggest beach club; we have not verified that claim. Entry is by day pass, with daybeds and sofas bookable separately.
best_for: A big lively day out or event with a group; sunset drinks in a large party setting
not_for: Guests wanting a small, quiet or intimate venue

name: Nook Umalas
why_its_here: Long-running open-air café/restaurant set beside Umalas rice fields, serving all-day Western and Indonesian food from breakfast to late (8am–11pm). Known as a calm rice-paddy escape a short hop from Seminyak's bustle.
best_for: relaxed rice-field brunch or breakfast; couples/groups wanting a calm all-day meal off the strip; vegetarian/vegan and gluten-free diners
not_for: anyone wanting a polished fine-dining or beachfront setting; nightlife seekers

name: Ji Restaurant Bali
why_its_here: Japanese-contemporary dining set in a reconstructed antique temple at Hotel Tugu, right on Batu Bolong beach, with a terrace and sweeping ocean views. Sushi, Asian-fusion plates and cocktails in one of Canggu's most atmospheric settings.
best_for: Sunset dinner with a view; date night; a special occasion by the sea.

name: Sensorium Bali
why_its_here: A daytime fusion cafe on Jl. Pantai Batu Mejan blending Australian cafe culture with Japanese-influenced flavours and minimalist design, from a chef with Australian fine-dining training.
best_for: A brunch or lunch of fusion cafe dishes in a calm, design-led room; a laptop-friendly daytime stop.
not_for: Dinner or late-night dining (it runs daytime hours only).

name: Fair Warung Balé
why_its_here: A social-enterprise warung on Jalan Sriwedari (Taman Kaja) run by the Fair Future Foundation/Bali Sari Foundation, where restaurant proceeds fund free medical consultations for the local community; serves Indonesian, Asian-fusion and vegetarian dishes daily.
best_for: Travellers wanting an easy, good-value Indonesian meal that also funds a local healthcare program; casual lunch or early dinner.
not_for: Diners seeking upscale fine dining or a view/sunset setting (a simple, ten-table warung).

name: Warung Mendez
why_its_here: A small warung tucked in Penestanan village northwest of central Ubud, run by an all-women kitchen team, serving Indonesian and Javanese-influenced dishes with an MSG-free, low-plastic ethos.
best_for: travelers wanting a quiet, home-style Indonesian meal off the main Ubud strip in Penestanan
not_for: those wanting a central, easy-to-find location right in town

name: Wulan Vegetarian Warung
why_its_here: A small, hole-in-the-wall all-vegan warung in the Peliatan area of Ubud, cash-only, serving an Indonesian menu of nasi goreng, tempeh, smoothies, and vegan sweets at very low prices.
best_for: budget-conscious vegan and vegetarian travelers wanting simple, authentic Indonesian dishes
not_for: diners wanting to pay by card or a polished sit-down setting — it's cash-only, floor-cushion seating

name: Bali Buda Ubud
why_its_here: Long-running Bali wholefoods institution (operating in Ubud since 1994) combining an organic grocery/bakery with an all-day restaurant covering raw vegan, Italian, and traditional Indonesian dishes.
best_for: Health-conscious travelers, longer-stay visitors, and mixed groups wanting a big menu with vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free options (including Bali's only gluten-free pizza base) in one place.
not_for: Travelers seeking an intimate fine-dining or special-occasion setting — it's a casual, functional health-food restaurant and shop.

name: Kilig - A Filipino Warung
where: F7GH+J43, Jl. Raya Goa Gajah No.94, Peliatan, Kecamatan Ubud, Kabupaten Gianyar, Bali 80582
why_its_here: A Filipino warung in Peliatan set in a bamboo hut with rice-field views, cooking home-style Filipino comfort food. It stands out as a dedicated Filipino kitchen in an area dominated by Balinese and Western menus.
best_for: filipino comfort food; calm rice-field setting; shared table meals; family dinner
not_for: a quick central-Ubud stop given the Peliatan location; anyone avoiding rich, pork-forward dishes
